young.match: Match each animal to what its baby is called.
young.odd: Three of these animals share a baby name: "{value}". Which one doesn't?
young.all: Tap all {n} animals whose babies are called "{value}".
young.reverse: Which of these animals has a baby called "{value}"?

rows.label: Cat
rows.hook: is the most popular household companion, famous for purring and for chasing mice and laser dots

rows.label: Dog
rows.description: domesticated mammal of the family Canidae
rows.hook: is called man's best friend, famous for loyalty, fetching sticks and wagging its tail

rows.label: Giant panda
rows.hook: is a black-and-white bamboo eater, the beloved symbol of a major wildlife conservation charity

rows.label: Capybara
rows.description: species of large semiaquatic rodent in the cavy family
rows.hook: is the world's largest rodent, a South American water-lover that other animals happily lounge on

rows.label: Lion
rows.hook: is the mane-sporting king of the jungle, living in prides on the African savanna

rows.label: Tiger
rows.hook: is the largest of the big cats, famous for its orange coat with black vertical stripes

rows.label: Wolf
rows.hook: is a pack-hunting canine famous for howling at the moon and starring in fairy tales as a big bad villain

rows.label: Horse
rows.description: domesticated four-footed mammal from the equine family
rows.hook: is a rideable, galloping animal long used for racing, farming and carrying knights into battle

rows.label: Jaguar
rows.description: species of big cat native to the Americas
rows.hook: is a spotted, powerful-jawed cat of the rainforests of Central and South America, and a carmaker's logo

rows.label: Polar bear
rows.description: species of bear native largely within the Arctic Circle
rows.hook: is a white-furred Arctic hunter that stalks seals on drifting sea ice

rows.label: Coyote
rows.hook: is a clever North American canine that yips at night and keeps escaping a cartoon predator's schemes

rows.label: Moose
rows.hook: is the largest member of the deer family, a huge antlered browser of northern forests

rows.label: Platypus
rows.description: semi-aquatic egg-laying mammal endemic to Australia
rows.hook: is a duck-billed, beaver-tailed Australian oddity that lays eggs yet nurses with milk

rows.label: Eel
rows.hook: is a slippery, snake-shaped fish that migrates across oceans to spawn in the Sargasso Sea

rows.label: Elephant
rows.description: large terrestrial mammals from Africa and Asia
rows.hook: is the largest land animal, famous for its trunk, tusks and a legendary memory

rows.label: Cheetah
rows.hook: is the fastest land animal, sprinting after prey in short bursts across the savanna

rows.label: Chicken
rows.description: domesticated bird (specifically a red junglefowl) kept by humans primarily as a food source
rows.hook: is the farmyard bird that lays breakfast eggs and is said to have crossed the road

rows.label: Cow
rows.hook: is the farm animal that gives milk and goes moo, held sacred in some cultures

rows.label: Brown bear
rows.hook: is a large, powerful omnivore of northern forests, known for catching salmon in rushing rivers

rows.label: Leopard
rows.hook: is a stealthy spotted cat that drags its kills up into trees, with a famous all-black variant

rows.label: Hippopotamus
rows.hook: is a huge, river-dwelling African mammal whose name means river horse, with a deadly wide-mouthed yawn

rows.label: Penguin
rows.description: family of birds in the order Sphenisciformes
rows.hook: is a flightless, tuxedo-looking bird that waddles on ice and swims like a torpedo

rows.label: Bat
rows.hook: is the only mammal capable of true flight, hanging upside down and navigating by echolocation

rows.label: Shark
rows.hook: is a toothy ocean predator whose dorsal fin made beachgoers fear the water in a blockbuster film

rows.label: Deer
rows.hook: is a graceful forest grazer whose males grow branching antlers, and a famous cartoon's Bambi

rows.label: Giraffe
rows.hook: is the tallest animal on Earth, with a famously long neck for munching treetop leaves

rows.label: Hamster
rows.hook: is a tiny pet rodent that stuffs its cheeks with food and runs for hours on a wheel

rows.label: Guinea pig
rows.hook: is a squeaky, cuddly pet rodent from the Andes, a classic classroom companion

rows.label: Kangaroo
rows.description: common name for some marsupials indigenous to Australia in the family Macropodidae
rows.hook: is a hopping Australian marsupial that carries its young in a pouch and can box

rows.label: Spider
rows.hook: is an eight-legged creature that spins silk webs to trap flies

rows.label: Koala
rows.description: arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia
rows.hook: is a sleepy Australian marsupial that clings to eucalyptus trees and munches their leaves

rows.label: Wild boar
rows.hook: is the tusked, bristly forest ancestor of the barnyard swine, famed in Asterix comics

rows.label: Pig
rows.hook: is a farm animal that oinks and rolls in mud, and the source of bacon and ham

rows.label: Beaver
rows.hook: is a dam-building rodent with a flat tail and big front teeth, the national emblem of Canada

rows.label: Echidna
rows.hook: is a spiny, egg-laying Australian mammal with a long sticky tongue for catching ants

rows.label: Goat
rows.description: domesticated mammal raised for its meat and milk
rows.hook: is a horned, hardy farm animal famous for climbing rocks, eating almost anything and giving milk for cheese

rows.label: Seal
rows.hook: is a flippered marine mammal that barks and basks on rocky shores, often balancing balls in circus acts

rows.label: Donkey
rows.description: subspecies of mammal (donkey as a domesticated subspecies); beast of burden, similar to a horse, but smaller
rows.hook: is a long-eared, stubborn beast of burden that brays and famously stars as Eeyore

rows.label: Sheep
rows.description: domesticated ruminant bred for meat, wool, and milk
rows.hook: is a woolly farm animal that goes baa, counted by insomniacs trying to fall asleep

rows.label: Frog
rows.description: order of short bodied, tailless amphibians
rows.hook: is a hopping, croaking amphibian, famed for kissing princes and for a green Muppet named Kermit

rows.label: Rhinoceros
rows.hook: is a thick-skinned giant with a horn on its nose, poached nearly to extinction

rows.label: Dolphin
rows.description: marine mammal, closely related to whales and porpoises
rows.hook: is a clever, playful ocean mammal known for leaping from the water and chattering in clicks and whistles

rows.label: Camel
rows.hook: is a hump-backed desert animal that can go long stretches without water, nicknamed the ship of the desert

rows.label: Crocodile
rows.hook: is a large armored reptile with powerful jaws that lurks in rivers, as in the Nile

rows.label: Hedgehog
rows.hook: is a small, spiky, insect-eating mammal that rolls into a ball when scared

rows.label: Peacock
rows.description: group of birds formed by the Indian peafowl, the green peafowl and the Congo peafowl
rows.hook: is a bird whose males fan out a dazzling blue-green tail of eyed feathers

rows.label: Otter
rows.hook: is a playful, sleek swimmer that floats on its back, holding hands with friends to avoid drifting apart

rows.label: Owl
rows.hook: is a nocturnal bird of prey with huge eyes, a swiveling head, and a reputation for wisdom

rows.label: Butterfly
rows.description: group of insects in the order Lepidoptera
rows.hook: is an insect that emerges from a chrysalis with colorful wings after starting life as a hungry crawler

rows.label: Bison
rows.hook: is a shaggy, humped giant of the American plains, once hunted to near extinction and shown on a nickel

rows.label: Reindeer
rows.hook: is the antlered animal said to pull a certain sleigh on Christmas Eve, led by one with a glowing red nose

rows.label: Duck
rows.description: common name for many species in the bird family Anatidae
rows.hook: is a web-footed water bird that quacks, and the species of Donald and Daffy

rows.label: Porcupine
rows.description: rodent with a coat of sharp spines
rows.hook: is a rodent with a coat of sharp quills it uses to defend itself against predators

rows.label: Pigeon
rows.hook: is a city-dwelling bird that coos in squares and once carried messages over long distances

rows.label: Zebra
rows.description: African subgenus of Equus of the horse family
rows.hook: is an African grazer famous for the bold black-and-white stripes that make each one unique

rows.label: Alpaca
rows.hook: is a fluffy, woolly South American camelid raised for soft fiber, sometimes known to spit

rows.label: Whale
rows.hook: is the largest animal ever, a giant ocean mammal that sings haunting songs and spouts from a blowhole

rows.label: Hare
rows.description: genus of mammals in the family Leporidae
rows.hook: is a long-eared, fast-running grassland animal that famously lost a race to a slow shelled opponent

rows.label: Llama
rows.hook: is a woolly Andean pack animal with a reputation for spitting when annoyed

rows.label: Ostrich
rows.hook: is the largest living bird, unable to fly but able to outrun most predators

rows.label: Water buffalo
rows.description: species of large bovid originating in South Asia

rows.label: Eagle
rows.hook: is a huge predatory bird of prey, many species of which hunt sizeable animals

rows.label: Flamingo
rows.hook: is a tall wading bird that is famous for its pink plumage and standing on one leg

rows.label: Sea lion
rows.hook: is an eared marine mammal with long front flippers that can walk on all fours on land

rows.label: Quail
rows.description: name for several genera of birds in the order Galliformes

rows.label: Turkey
rows.description: North American genus of large birds
rows.hook: is a heavy, ground-dwelling bird with a fleshy wattle, and a traditional holiday dinner in North America

rows.label: Goose
rows.description: common name for a group of birds
rows.hook: is a large waterfowl whose female shares its name with the male, called a gander

rows.label: Swan
rows.hook: is the largest waterfowl, an elegant long-necked bird that often mates for life

rows.label: Sea turtle
rows.hook: is a marine reptile with a shell and flippers, including the green, hawksbill and leatherback kinds
